_source: LOCAL finetune: /home/rohit/pretrained_model_lid_v1 (lerobot 'smolvla' type, ckpt 004000 of smolvla_lid_pickup_v1, trained by Omer Kirnap). SAME ARCHITECTURE as the smolvla variant -- 500 tensors, same keys, same shapes. NON-QG LANE: its config.json names the STOCK backbone (HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct, pretrained_path smolvla_base-*), so the vision activation it was trained on is SigLIP's gelu_pytorch_tanh, NOT the quick_gelu the FPGA LALU computes. It therefore stays OUT of NATIVE_QUICK_GELU: --hw-gelu is a gate-sharpening substitution here, not the honest oracle. Selected with --variant smolvla_lid.

fixed_isa_regs._budget: 15 GPRs total; 1-9 fixed here, 10-15 free for rope/flash scratch. The M regs are the gpr_M_reg handles for the vision/lm/expert PBI matmul loops -- declared so the budget stays visible.

vision._stack: SigLIP v1 vision tower (SiglipVisionTransformer, exported as SmolVLMVisionTransformer, model_type smolvlm_vision), derived from google/siglip-base-patch16-512. Weights under vis.*. Identified by tensor signature: no CLS token (pos_embed 1024 == 32x32 exactly), post_layernorm but no pre_layrnorm (rules out CLIP), out_proj naming, fc1/fc2 non-gated MLP. No attention-pooling head (vision_use_head=False) -- the connector needs all 1024 patch tokens.
vision._image_splitting: Upstream SmolVLM2 sets do_image_splitting=true (tile a <=2048px image into up to 16 512x512 tiles + a thumbnail, up to 1088 image tokens). Verapulse does NOT exercise it: predict_example passes (B,3,512,512) per camera, already one tile at native tower resolution. So 1 image -> 1024 patches -> 64 tokens per camera, fixed shape, no variable tile count. Confirm the preprocessing does not prepend a per-camera thumbnail.
vision._num_image_slots_note: 2, NOT the 3 that the checkpoint's config.json input_features lists. The dataset (dataset_meta/info.json) has exactly two cameras -- 'high' and 'wrist', 44 episodes / 25949 frames -- renamed to camera1/camera2. camera3 is declared but never supplied, and modeling_smolvla.prepare_images only materializes a zero-filled substitute while `num_empty_cameras < config.empty_cameras`; empty_cameras is 0, so that loop breaks on its first iteration and NO third image is ever appended. The model therefore saw two images in training and must see two at inference: the prefix is genuinely shorter, not zero-padded. Native frames are 3x256x256, resize_imgs_with_padding=[512,512] brings them to the tower's 512, so every tower dim below is unchanged.

connector._stack: pixel-shuffle x4 then one linear, weights under conn.*
connector._note: shuffle folds a 4x4 patch block into channels: 768*16 = 12288 -> 960. Emit it as smart_bf16_permute_core(dims=[8,4,8,4,768], permute_indices=[0,2,1,3,4]) then a plain M=64 K=12288 N=960 matmul -- exactly smolvlm2_test.py:597-607. Natively supported, DMA-gather path, no weight pre-permute needed.

lm._stack: SmolLM2-360M-class VLM decoder, weights under lm.*
lm._rope_theta_note: 10000.0 -- READ FROM THE CODE, NOT FROM config.json. SmolVLA does NOT use HF's rotary embedding: smolvlm_with_expert.py defines its own `apply_rope(x, positions, max_wavelength=10_000)` and forward_attn_layer calls it with NO theta argument, so the hardcoded 10000 wins for BOTH the prefix and the action expert. The backbone's text_config.rope_theta=100000 (HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct) is real but DEAD -- nothing reads it. Setting 100000 from that config cost a debugging session: vision and the assembled prefix input both gated 32 dB against upstream while the very first prefix layer's K cache collapsed to cos 0.738, because K is the first tensor that gets rotated. Rotation CONVENTION matches ours (split-half, x1*cos - x2*sin). For a custom checkpoint, the code is ground truth over the config.
lm._num_layers_note: 16, from the checkpoint's num_vlm_layers. SmolVLA TRUNCATES the 32-layer backbone and the safetensors carries exactly text_model.layers.0..15.

expert._stack: action expert, 0.75x VLM width, weights under ae.* (upstream lm_expert.*)
expert._kv_match: expert kv_out 320 == lm kv_out 320 by construction (same 5 kv heads x hd 64), so the frozen VLM prefix KV cache drops into the expert's attention geometry with no reshaping. It does NOT mean the cache is used unprojected: cross-attention layers RE-PROJECT it through their own k_proj/v_proj first. The checkpoint proves it -- expert.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.weight is (320,720) (self: expert hidden width 720) while expert.layers.1.self_attn.k_proj.weight is (320,320) (cross: the VLM kv width). No RoPE is applied to the reprojected K (the cache already carries the prefix rotation); the expert query is roped with positions rebased to 0..chunk-1.
expert._layer_mode_note: layer i self-attends when i % 2 == 0, else cross-attends onto the frozen VLM prefix K/V. NOW VERIFIED for this checkpoint by tensor shape: even layers have self_attn.k_proj [320,720] (expert width), odd layers [320,320] (VLM kv width).
expert._layer_count_note: num_expert_layers 0 means 'match the VLM'; the checkpoint has lm_expert.layers.0..15. intermediate_size 2048 is READ FROM THE CHECKPOINT (mlp.gate/up [2048,720]), not derived -- 2560*0.75 = 1920 would be wrong.

action_head._flow: x_t = t*noise + (1-t)*a; expert predicts v; Euler with dt = -1/num_steps. action_in_proj(32->720) || time_emb(720) -> concat 1440 -> action_time_mlp_in(1440->720) -> silu -> action_time_mlp_out(720->720) -> expert 16 layers -> ae.final_norm(720) -> action_out_proj(720->32), take [:, :6].
action_head._precompute_limit: Only the RAW sinusoid [10,480] is precomputable on the host. pi05's trick of precomputing the WHOLE conditioning table does NOT transfer: there the time MLP was standalone and input-independent, whereas action_time_mlp_in here consumes concat(action_in_proj(x_t), time_emb) and x_t changes every Euler step. Everything from action_time_mlp_in onward runs on device, per step.
action_head._n_action_steps_note: n_action_steps is 50 here (the WHOLE chunk is executed before re-planning), while num_denoise_steps is 10. In the pulsevla variant both were 10 and the coincidence was a footgun; here they differ, which is the safer configuration to reason about.

model._prefix_note: 1 state token + 2*64 image tokens + 48 text = 177 -> pad to 192 (3*64). Pad rows must be masked via the attention bias tensor AND excluded from every SNR probe. At 2 slots PREFILL_MAX_SEQ_LEN (192) again equals AE_FLASH_ROWS (SUFFIX_LEN_PAD 64 x GROUP_SIZE 3), so the expert's conditional regs['pm'] is not allocated and the flash borrows regs['qb'] exactly as pulsevla does -- see project-verapulse-qb-pm-coincidence. That collision is still a coincidence, not an invariant; the conditional code stays.
model._OPEN_prefix_layout: BLOCKING, resolve from the reference before compiling the prefix. (a) image_token_id 49190 exists, which implies image embeddings are SCATTERED into placeholder positions inside the tokenized text sequence (the SmolVLM/SmolVLA pattern), NOT concatenated in front of it. If so the prefix is not state||images||text at all, and both the length and every RoPE position change. (b) The state token is assumed at row 0, but pi0/pi0.5 and SmolVLA put state LAST (images -> language -> state). (c) Upstream config says prefix_length: 0, unexplained and contradicting prefix_len 177.
model._OPEN_valid_len: valid prefix length is NOT the constant 177: tokenizer_max_length 48 means text is PADDED to 48, so the real count is 1 + 128 + n_real_text and varies per prompt. Masking only rows 177..191 would treat the padded text tokens inside rows 129..176 as valid, corrupting attention and -- via cumsum -- every downstream RoPE position. RoPE positions must be cumsum(attention_mask), not arange (the pi05 lesson).
model._OPEN_expert_rope: (a) suffix RoPE positions: SmolVLA continues them from the prefix (prefix_len .. prefix_len+49), not 0..49. (b) on cross-attn layers, is Q rotated at all, and against which base, given K comes from the prefix cache already rotated with prefix positions? (c) does cross layer i read LM layer i's KV or the final-layer KV? All three are undefined and all three read as generic drift if wrong.
model._OPEN_layer_parity: self-attn assumed on i % 2 == 0. If inverted, all 32 expert layers are wrong in a way that looks like drift, not a structural bug.

ops._causal_removed: there is no single causal flag for this model: vision is bidirectional, the prefix is a BLOCK mask (not uniformly bidirectional -- image+state block vs language follow different rules), and the expert mixes bidirectional-within-chunk self-attn with full cross-attn. Every mask is an explicit precomputed bias tensor derived from the reference.
ops._quant_note: bring up every stack in bf16 first (pi05 lesson: chained IF4 allocations gave -2.97 dB). Flip to q4_64 per-stack only after that stack passes >=40 dB.

dram_layout._note_layout: Bases are OFFSETS from DRAM_START_ADDR=0x80000000, and are DELIBERATELY the same as the pulsevla variant's. 450.05M params (exact, from the safetensors) = 900 MB bf16 before pads vs pulsevla's 559M/1.132 GB, so params_end moves DOWN to ~0x3B000000 and the existing tensor base at 0x48000000 gains headroom rather than losing it. _assert_params_fit is the check that matters; do not hand-tune these until it complains. Program arena stays 2.85 GB, and this variant needs LESS of it: 16 layers not 32 halves both the prefix flash count and the 160 (was 320) expert flash calls.

reference._note: The whole VLM half of this model is ALREADY brought up and HW-validated in this repo. Reuse it; do not re-derive.
reference.vision_port_plan: TAKE pi05's ENCODER STRUCTURE + smolvlm2's CONSTANTS AND PERMUTES. pi05's compile_encoder is itself descended from smolvlm2 (its docstring: 'Structure follows the proven smolvlm2_test.py section 7 shared-subroutine-flash pattern') and adds what smolvlm2 lacks: multi-engine sharding over rows AND a K-axis grid (_emit_encoder_body(ue, engine_idx, sched, row_offset, rows, kgrp, nk); 202 multi-engine refs vs smolvlm2's 0). smolvlm2 supplies what pi05 cannot: the exact dims (768/12x64/3072/1024 patches/patch16) and both permutes (patch-embed reorder + scale-4 pixel shuffle, which pi05 has no equivalent of -- its connector is scale 1 = identity). Retarget pi05's loop bounds 27->12 layers, S 256->1024, H 1152->768, NH 16->12, I 4304->3072.
reference.hd72_deletes_cleanly: pi05's head_dim 72->128 pad is NOT a stage to unpick: it lives in the WEIGHT STORE (_pad_proj, pi05_libero_test.py:605-624) with every downstream buffer DP=128 wide. At head_dim 64, D == DP == 64, so _pad_proj collapses to identity and the buffers become 64-wide. A 64-element slice is 128 B, still AXI-beat (32 B) aligned. Pure simplification -- and it removes the known-broken hd=72 flash path rather than importing it.
reference.patch_embed_permute: smolvlm2_test.py:536-543 does the patch-embed channel-major reorder ON DEVICE: smart_bf16_permute_core(dims=[3,32,16,32,16], permute_indices=[1,3,0,2,4]) then matmat_mul_core(M=1024,K=768,N=768, bias_mode='broadcast_N', gpr_M_reg=vis_S_reg). Taking this path makes the 'host patchify must emit (c,kh,kw) order or it is finite-but-scrambled' hazard moot.
reference.swin_is_wrong_shape: swin's patch merging is a scale-2 2x2 spatial->channel fold. This model needs scale 4. Use smolvlm2's, not swin's.
reusable_verbatim: SmolVLM2_UnifiedEngine.compile_encoder  -- identical ViT (12x768, 12 heads, hd 64, MHA) + pixel-shuffle x4 connector (12288->960)
SmolVLM2_UnifiedEngine._load_rope_tables -- same theta/head_dim; note it uses 100000.0
SmolVLM2_UnifiedEngine.weight_init q4_64 path for the vision + lm stacks
compile_prefill's duplicate_gqa_rows -- the 5->15 K/V row replication flash needs for GQA group 3
must_change_from_smolvlm2: prefix attention is BIDIRECTIONAL over the observation, not causal decode
no LM head / sampling / stop tokens -- output is continuous actions
the prefix must PERSIST per-layer K/V [192,320] x32 as the expert's cross-attn source
prefix rows now include a state token and 2 camera slots (128 image tokens), not 1
take_from_pi05: file/stage structure, compile-once + bins, prefix-KV dump for oracle isolation
action-expert + flow-matching denoise loop shape, precomputed timestep table
per-stage SNR gating with masked rows excluded

paths._ckpt_note: LOCAL checkpoint, not an HF repo -- ensure_checkpoint() returns local_ckpt_dir as-is and downloads nothing. Delivered by scp from okirnap:/home/okirnap/work/train_robot3/outputs/smolvla_lid_pickup_v1/checkpoints/004000/pretrained_model/ -- no fetch script, no HF mirror; this directory is the only copy. Re-request from Omer if lost.
paths._tokenizer_note: the finetune package ships NO tokenizer.json; upstream pulls the processor from the backbone repo at load time, so we do the same.
paths._norm_stats_note: REGENERATED, not shipped: the delivered pretrained_model/ carries no normalization_stats.json, only the lerobot processor safetensors. Rebuilt from policy_preprocessor_step_5_normalizer_processor.safetensors into the sibling variants' schema. NOT INTERCHANGEABLE with theirs -- different task and dataset, and the stats moved materially (state mean[2] 18.59 -> 42.79, mean[4] 4.73 -> -46.38). Using another variant's file denormalizes every action against the wrong distribution: plausible motion, consistently wrong, and nothing raises. VISUAL is IDENTITY (uint8/255 only); STATE and ACTION are MEAN_STD.
paths._ckpt_num_tensors_note: 499 MAPPED, from 500 in the file: vlm.lm_head.weight [49280,960] is in _IGNORED_KEYS. SmolVLA's output is continuous actions, so there is no token head -- the pulsevla export omits it entirely, this one ships it unused.

hw_notes: ATTENTION KINDS (settled against the SmolVLM2-500M reference, not just the checkpoint shapes): vision = MHA, 12 q heads / 12 kv heads, hd 64. lm = GQA, 15 q / 5 kv, group 3, hd 64. expert = GQA, 15 q / 5 kv, group 3, hd 64. NOTHING here is MQA (that is pi05, num_kv_heads=1) -- do not reuse pi05's MQA attention emitters.

GQA on this HW: flash wants matching q/kv head counts, so the 5 kv heads must be row-replicated to 15 before the flash call. models/smolvlm2/smolvlm2_test.py::compile_prefill already has this as duplicate_gqa_rows -- reuse it rather than re-deriving. The alternative (rope_hf_core_dram_gqa) applies to the rope step, where hd 64 -> half 32 is exactly 32-aligned, so it is usable directly at N=64.

The observation is 2 cameras (camera1=high, camera2=wrist), from dataset_meta/info.json -- the checkpoint config.json's third entry (camera3) is never supplied and prepare_images does not synthesize it at empty_cameras=0. 2 slots divides the engine counts this box can offer (8 % 2 == 0), so _vis_batch_plan CAN batch both slots at ne>=4 and even -- unlike the 3-slot case, which needed ne divisible by 3.

GOOD NEWS vs pi05/MoonViT: every attention head_dim here is 64 -- vision 768/12=64, lm 960/15=64, expert 960/15=64. No 72->128 pad, no unpad selection matrix, no pre-scale. The known-broken hd=72 flash path is NOT on this model's critical path.

THE 720 PROBLEM (the sibling variant's '480 problem' at a different width): expert hidden_size 720 is NOT a multiple of 64 (720/64 = 11.25), so it violates both the 64-ALU floor and the 128B SRAM row quantum. Pad the expert hidden dim to 768 everywhere: K-pad (zero rows) on q/k/v/gate/up weights, N-pad (zero cols) on o_proj/down_proj/action_in_proj/action_time_mlp_* outputs. Bake the pad into the STORED weights (the reformat is a weight), never into a runtime staging copy. The emitter already derives every one of these from hidden_size/hidden_size_padded, so this is a config change, not a code change.

RMSNorm over the padded 768 is NOT the same as over 720: the mean-square denominator changes. Because RMS has no mean subtraction, zero pad lanes leave the numerator untouched and only rescale the denominator by a known constant, so folding it into the stored gamma works. THE CONSTANT IS gamma' = gamma * sqrt(720/768) = gamma * 0.968246 -- NUMERICALLY THE SAME FACTOR AS THE SIBLING'S sqrt(480/512), because 480/512 and 720/768 are both 15/16. Coincidence, not a shared derivation: the code computes math.sqrt(H/HP) and must keep doing so. Direction still matters -- normalizing over 768 instead of 720 makes the denominator SMALLER, so the kernel's output is LARGER by sqrt(768/720) and gamma must scale DOWN. Over this variant's 33 expert norms (16 layers x2 + final) the reciprocal would compound ~1e5x. Assert the pad lanes are still zero after every expert op.

The 720->768 pad BREAKS the action_time_mlp_in concat. That weight is [720,1440] with K=1440 = concat(action_in_proj_out[720], time_emb[720]). Once both halves are 768-padded the second half starts at column 768, not 720, so a K=1440 matmul reads the wrong columns for the entire time half. Keeping the concat contiguous at 1440 is ILLEGAL: the time half would start at byte 1440, not a multiple of 128. FIX: K-pad action_time_mlp_in 1440 -> 1536, permuting its input columns so source [0:720] sits at [0:720] and source [720:1440] sits at [768:1488], zeros elsewhere. Combined with the N-pad, the stored weight is [768, 1536]. _weight_init_head already writes this split symbolically in terms of H and HP -- verified, no edit needed.

Head BIASES need the same padding as their weights: state_proj.bias[960] is clean, but action_in_proj.bias[720], action_time_mlp_in.bias[720], action_time_mlp_out.bias[720] must be zero-padded to 768 and action_out_proj.bias[32] to 64. A bias write into the pad lanes poisons the zero-pad invariant the RMSNorm fold depends on. The expert stack itself is bias-free.
The precomputed timestep table must be [10, 768], not [10, 720] -- innermost dim must be %64 so a row DMAs into the padded slot without a sub-row copy.

Expert q_out=960, kv_out=320, intermediate=2048 are all multiples of 64 -- only the 720 residual stream needs padding. head_dim 64 means GQA rope halves are 32 elements = exactly 32-aligned, so rope_hf_core_dram_gqa is usable directly at N=64.

Vision is the compute hog: image 512 / patch 16 = 32x32 = 1024 tokens PER IMAGE, x2 cameras, x12 layers, bidirectional flash at seq 1024 hd 64. This dominates latency, and it is the natural first multi-engine target (row-split over the 1024 tokens, shard once at chain entry, single barrier before attention needs joined K/V).

Vision MLP activation is gelu_pytorch_tanh: 0.5*x*(1+tanh(sqrt(2/pi)*(x+0.044715*x^3))), the SigLIP default, within ~1e-3 of exact erf-GELU. The HW GELU is the SIGMOID approximation x*sigmoid(1.702*x) (user_dma_core.py:299, LALU_ACT_GELU_B=0xbfd9=-1.702), which deviates from true GELU by up to ~0.02 absolute around |x| in [2,3]. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (1) the CPU oracle must use the SIGMOID form when scoring HW-vs-oracle, or every vision MLP stage falsely reads ~28 dB low; (2) the substitution is a real model-vs-reality approximation that belongs in the vision error budget -- it is not exact. models/smolvlm2/smolvlm2_test.py:592 already ships this substitution (gelu_enable=True) and passed its gate, so it is empirically tolerable at this depth. (Near-miss trivia: x*sigmoid(1.702x) IS exactly CLIP's quick_gelu -- if this tower were CLIP the HW would be bit-right.)
Vision attention has bias on q/k/v/out_proj and the LayerNorms have bias; the LM/expert stacks are bias-free RMSNorm. Do not copy pi05's bias-free vision assumptions.

The connector pixel-shuffle is NATIVELY SUPPORTED -- do not hand-roll it and do not pre-permute the weight. models/smolvlm2/smolvlm2_test.py:597-607 does this exact op in one call: smart_bf16_permute_core(dims=[8,4,8,4,768], permute_indices=[0,2,1,3,4], in=VIS_POST_LN_DRAM, out=VIS_SHUFFLED_DRAM), then matmat_mul_core(M=64, K=12288, N=960) reads the shuffled buffer directly (reshape is free in a flat address space). dims views the 1024 tokens as (by,dy,bx,dx); the perm reorders to (by,bx,dy,dx), whose row-major flattening IS 64x12288. It is CHEAP because the last dim 768 stays put and is 64-aligned, so nn_lib.py:168-205 takes Case 1, a pure DMA GATHER: per-output-row memcpy with the source offset from a precomputed index table, destination written sequentially. The moving unit is a whole 768-element row = 1536 B = 12 full SRAM rows, so no sub-row addressing and NO per-index destination offset -- the strided-copy footgun does not apply here. Cost: 1024 small memcpys + 8 bulk writes of static program. Precedent at scale 2: locateanything_3b_test.py:4642 (Qwen2.5-VL merger), same [0,2,1,3,4] family. The known smart_bf16_permute_core bug (transpose path, N_transpose > 64) is Case 2 and does not touch this. A host round-trip is possible but wrong: 3 MB each way per camera, and it splits the encoder's single captured program, forfeiting compile-once.

NO SITE IN THIS MODEL NEEDS ONLINE TRIG, and the ISA could not provide it anyway: the LALU exposes exp/sigmoid/silu/gelu/tanh but has NO sine or cosine primitive to lower onto (pi05 _ae_compile_cond_table). Vision pos-embed is a learned lookup with no interpolation (SmolVLM buckets patch coords to integer ids; at fixed 512px it collapses to arange(1024)). LM RoPE, expert RoPE (positions arange(50)), and the 10-step timestep sinusoid are all host-precomputed tables baked into params.bin. Data-dependent prefix positions do NOT break this: the table is indexed BY POSITION VALUE, so one static [S_max,64] table serves every prompt and only the gather indices vary. Flow matching is linear/optimal-transport (x_t = t*noise + (1-t)*a) -- no beta or cosine noise schedule exists to worry about.

SILU TRAP on the time MLP: pi05 measured -6 dB on exactly this tensor using fused silu_enable=True (the LALU's piecewise-approximate SiLU). The fix was composed silu_core_dram -- true x*sigmoid(x) via identity-matmul sigmoid + elementwise multiply. verapulse CANNOT dodge it by precomputing (action_time_mlp_in consumes x_t, which changes every Euler step), so the action_time_mlp_in -> silu -> action_time_mlp_out chain must run on device per step: use the composed SiLU there and score it against a host oracle.

PROGRAM SIZE is the real budget risk, not weights. A naive unroll emits 24 vision flashes (12 layers x 2 slots at seq 1024) + 16 prefix flashes + 16 expert layers x 10 denoise steps = 160 expert flashes. Swin's static flash alone was 103 MB before staging. Use the proven in-tree fix: compile flash ONCE as a subroutine (gpr_ret_id + jump_abs, return via JUMP_REG_ABS) and memcpy-stage each call's Q/K/V into its fixed buffers -- memcpy-style PBI injection DOES re-execute correctly (swin 103MB -> 9.4MB; gemma3 re-executes static flash thousands of times). Separately, roll the 10 Euler steps into ONE compiled body (gpr_M_reg + an advancing pointer into the timestep table) instead of a Python for-loop: the loop is static, but unrolling it is a 10x program multiplier.

RoPE at N=64 is legal but PBI-ONLY (verified in user_dma_core.py): rope_hf_core_dram dispatches to rope_hf_core_dram_dynamic when gpr_M_reg is passed, and that path's padded-split branch asserts only 0 < N < 128 (N bytes = 128 is beat-aligned). A BARE call with no GPR falls through to rope_hf_core_dram_legacy, which asserts N >= 128 (line 4169); rope_hf_core_dram_gqa and the decode core assert N >= 128 AND N % 128 == 0. smolvlm2's compile_prefill already runs N=64 in production. So: always pass gpr_M_reg, never use the _gqa variant at this head_dim -- do the group broadcast with duplicate_gqa_rows instead.

Post-residual norms (twice per layer, 32 of them across lm+expert) map to layer_norm_core_dram_post_add, which has NO PBI and is a proven dead end (4 advancing pointers vs the <=3 limit; wiring it broke qwen-vl and saved 2 MB). They stay STATIC -- budget that program cost. Note also that the LM/expert use rms_norm_core_dram whose gpr_M_reg is M, while layer_norm_core_dram's is M//chunk_size (chunk COUNT); crossing the two is silent. The vision stack needs true LayerNorm WITH bias -- confirm layer_norm_core_dram accepts a beta operand before planning on it.

Cross-attention layers reuse the FROZEN VLM prefix K/V, so the prefix runs once per observation and the 10 denoise steps only re-run the expert. Cache prefix K/V in DRAM exactly like pi05 does; self-attention layers (i%2==0) additionally build the expert's own K/V over the 50-token action chunk each step.

The 10-step Euler loop is a fixed schedule (dt = -1/10, t known at compile time), so the whole denoise loop can be compiled once with all 10 timestep embeddings precomputed on the host (input-independent subcomputation -- do NOT run the sinusoid through fused kernels).

PBI: use gpr_M_reg on matmat_mul_core for the 16 expert layers x 10 steps (M=64) to keep the program bin small; layer_norm_core_dram's reg is chunk COUNT not M; keep flash static/legacy (PBI flash address injection corrupts on the 2nd execution).
Suffix length 50 pads to 64 = exactly one 64-row tile: convenient, but the 14 pad rows must be masked in the attention bias and excluded from every SNR.

Engine-construction hazard: any UnifiedEngine built after weight_init DMA-writes 16KB of noise to 0x80000000. Build the scheduler/workers BEFORE weight_init, or snapshot 0x80000000..+64KB into a bfloat16 buffer and restore.

Correctness gate: >=40 dB SNR vs the pure-torch reference, per stage (vision layer 0 -> vision out -> connector -> prefix layer 0 -> prefix out -> expert step 0 -> actions). Masked/pad rows excluded. 'No NaN' is not correctness. NOTE the measured bf16 ceiling: vision/prefix cap near ~28 dB on deep stacks, so use per-stage thresholds plus cosine similarity rather than a flat 40 dB. This variant's stacks are HALF as deep as the sibling's, so the ceiling should be friendlier here -- measure it, do not assume it.

ACTION SPACE IS SO-101, NOT LIBERO: 6 real joints (shoulder_pan, shoulder_lift, elbow_flex, wrist_flex, wrist_roll, gripper) sliced from the 32-wide padded head. Units are normalized (MEAN_STD via normalization_stats.json), NOT degrees; the robot client is launched with --robot.use_degrees=false. Do not reuse LIBERO's 7-DoF unnormalization.

CHECKPOINT DTYPE IS MIXED: 474 BF16 / 26 F32 tensors (the trained action head, state_proj, and every cross-attn k/v pair). This is NOT a problem -- load_state_dict casts everything to float32 and store_weight casts to bf16 on the way to params DRAM, and assert_bf16_only only inspects config ops[*_quant], never tensor dtypes. Noted because it reads like a blocker and is not one.
